THE MEASURE OF SPACE

Real geometry. Explicit scale.

One scene unit is one astronomical unit: 149,597,870.7 km. TRUE SCALE uses that same conversion for every diameter, distance, and orbit. VISIBLE PLANETS gives planets (including Pluto) a minimum screen radius of 7 pixels; centers and orbital paths are unchanged. The Sun remains at physical size. In TRUE SCALE, each body is represented by either its physical sphere or one hollow marker at its projected center, never both. Spheres below 2 CSS pixels in projected diameter are hidden; markers switch back to spheres at 2.2 pixels to prevent flicker. Text labels have no duplicate dot or connector. VISIBLE PLANETS retains its existing label markers and leaders.

A fixed, measured moment

Body-center geometric positions and osculating elements from NASA/JPL Horizons, at 2026-09-27 00:00 TDB. Heliocentric, J2000 ecliptic frame; no light-time correction. This is a dated snapshot, not a live or animated ephemeris. The paths are instantaneous Keplerian ellipses, not long-term perturbed trajectories.

Planets are spheres using JPL volume-equivalent mean radii; oblateness, rings, surface features, and moons are not modeled. Sun radius: IAU nominal 695,700 km. Body colors are identifiers. IAU 2015 resolution B3 · AU definition.

Numerical verification

BodyDiameter / Eartha / Eartha (AU)ei (°)

Ratios use this epoch’s osculating semi-major axes. Inclination is relative to the J2000 ecliptic. Floating-point and line tessellation have finite precision; input geometry is never compressed or exaggerated.
